name: LinuxMaster Image Generator for ComfyUI
author: linuxmaster1989

sections.description:
span_3LinuxMaster Image Generator for ComfyUI allows you to seamlessly integrate a self-hosted ComfyUI server with your WordPress website, enabling users to generate images directly from the front-end or back-end using defined workflows.span_3

🌟 Features

  • span_4Remote Generation: Send prompts and parameters from WordPress to your remote ComfyUI server.span_4
  • span_5Workflow Integration: Utilizes a pre-defined ComfyUI workflow (configured via JSON) for consistent results.span_5
  • span_6Shortcode Integration: Easily embed the image generation interface anywhere on your site using a simple shortcode.span_6

⚙️ Setup and Configuration

  1. span_7ComfyUI Server Setup: Ensure your ComfyUI server is running and accessible via a secure, public URL.span_7 span_8You will need the API endpoint.span_8
  2. Workflow Preparation:
    • span_9Create or load your desired workflow in the ComfyUI interface.span_9
    • span_10The node intended for the main text prompt must be renamed to 1 (one) for the plugin to correctly inject the user’s positive prompt.span_10
    • span_11Export the workflow as a JSON file for configuration within the plugin settings.span_11
  3. Plugin Configuration: Access the plugin settings page to input:
    • span_12Your ComfyUI Server URL.span_12
    • span_13The necessary API key (if applicable).span_13
    • span_14The contents of your prepared workflow JSON.span_14

💻 Usage

To display the image generation form on any post or page, simply use the following shortcode:

span_15[COMFYUI_GENERATOR]span_15

span_16Users will input their desired prompt, and the request will be sent to your ComfyUI server based on the configured workflow.span_16

⚠️ Plugin Technical Requirements

span_17This plugin requires specific server configurations for the external ComfyUI server to function properly.span_17 span_18This is not for a shared hosting environment.span_18

  • span_19Server OS: UBUNTU 22.04 LTS (or newer) with FULL ROOT/SSH ACCESS is required for the self-hosted ComfyUI server.span_19
  • span_20SSL Certificate Path: sudo nano /etc/nginx/ssl/comfyui.crt (or equivalent steps).span_20
  • span_21Workflow Setup: RENAME POSITIVE PROMPT NODE TO 1 in the ComfyUI API JSON.span_21
  • span_22Browser Requirement: Ensure your web browser is up-to-date and supports the necessary connection protocols for the plugin interface.span_22

🤝 Credits

span_23Special thanks to Jesse Karban for contributions to the development and architecture of this integration.span_23
sections.installation:
1. span_24Upload the linuxmaster-image-generator-for-comfyui folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.span_24
  2. span_25Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.span_25
  3. span_26Configure the plugin settings with your ComfyUI server details and prepared workflow JSON.span_26
  4. span_27Use the shortcode [COMFYUI_GENERATOR] on any page or post.span_27
sections.faq:
Q: Why do I need to rename the Positive Prompt node to ‘1’?

span_28A: This is a requirement of the plugin’s API implementation to correctly identify and inject the user-provided prompt into your custom ComfyUI workflow JSON structure.span_28

Q: Where can I find my ComfyUI workflow JSON?

span_29A: In the ComfyUI web interface, right-click on the canvas and select “Save (API Format)”.span_29 span_30This JSON file contains the blueprint for your generation.span_30
